Subject: Sunrise Therapeutics — Private deployment readiness & 2-week implementation runway

Hi Alex / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a short, actionable runbook in your inbox so we can align schedules and owners for the initial implementation sprint (target window: 2026-12-07 through 2026-12-20). High level goals:

- Establish VPC peering and test private endpoints
- Deliver and smoke-test the on-prem package in your staging rack
- Verify certs / KMS / audit log delivery for compliance team
- Run a short load smoke test (50 qps sustained) and validate latency SLOs

Immediate asks from Sunrise:
1) Confirm two 90-minute windows next week for an initial peering session (we suggest 2026-12-07 16:00 PST or 2026-12-08 10:00 PST).
2) Share the network diagram and preferred CIDR ranges for peering (we referenced a basic diagram in the CNF yesterday, but we need the formal VPC map).
3) Confirm whether you require HSM/KMS integration (we support customer-managed KMS via our Private control plane).

Attached: redwood_private_deploy_requirements_v1.pdf (overview + port matrix + install checklist).

Proposed owners (happy to adjust):
- Network / peering: Rajiv (Sunrise) + Marissa (Redwood)
- On-prem package installation: Dev (Redwood) + Tom Walters (consultant)
- Compliance / certs: Alex (Sunrise) + Stephanie (Redwood)

I'll follow up with a brief agenda for the peering session once you confirm a time.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attaching our VPC map and a short network summary. Quick details that will matter for the peering session:

- VPC CIDR (prod): 10.20.0.0/16
- Staging CIDR: 10.21.0.0/16
- Preferred peering: static route peering (no BGP) — we prefer simple static routes for the first rollout
- Firewall (east-west) allowlist: 443/tcp, 50051/tcp (gRPC), 9200/tcp (metrics), 514/udp (syslog) — we will open 10.21.0.0/16 -> Redwood peering CIDR only
- Egress for smoke tests will originate from 35.227.44.12 (please allow this IP)
- Proposed maintenance window for peering: 2026-12-07 16:00–18:00 PST (matches Jonas' suggestion)

Attachment: sunrise_vpc_network_map.png (png, 180KB stub)

One question for Redwood: do you require an active BGP session for route health, or will you honor static routes advertised from our routing table?

—Rajiv

Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem package notes + proposed sprint tasks

Thanks for the context — a few technical notes from the install side and a compact sprint checklist we can use in the peering session.

On-prem package and delivery:
- Installer: offline bundle (redwood_onprem_package_v2.tar.gz) — includes container images, helm chart, and an offline install script.
- Disk footprint: ~18GB compressed, ~52GB expanded on node (we recommend provisioning 80GB for logs/metrics).
- Typical runtime: requires at least 2 worker nodes with GPUs (NVIDIA A10 or better) for inference; single-node dev install supported without GPUs for functional testing.
- KMS: we support both software-based KMS (initial) and HSM via KMIP/HSM integration for production. For compliance, we recommend HSM in prod; software KMS is fine for initial staging.

Ports & behavior (to share with security):
- 443/tcp (API + private endpoint TLS)
- 50051/tcp (gRPC control plane)
- 9200/tcp (metrics, Prometheus scrape)
- 514/udp (syslog forward)
- 2049/tcp (NFS, if you choose NFS-backed model cache)

Proposed 2-week sprint (roles & owners):
- Day 0: Network prep & peering session (Rajiv + Marissa)
- Day 1–2: Cert issuance & KMS prep (Alex + Stephanie)
- Day 3–4: Preload installer on staging rack (Tom + Dev)
- Day 5: Install & smoke test (Dev + Marissa + Tom)
- Day 6–10: Validation tests, performance tuning, and rollback exercises (Dev + Marissa)

Attachments: redwood_onprem_package_v2.tar.gz (archive, 18GB stub)

Open questions we should cover on the call:
1) Route preference: static only or initial static with optional BGP later?
2) Are you planning to use NFS for the model cache or local ephemeral storage?
3) Who will own cert issuance (Sunrise CA vs. Redwood temporary cert)?

Happy to own the installation run and the smoke test checklist — will bring a step-by-step runbook to the call.

—Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Installations
Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
